records.rule: First model the state, identity, authority and invariants in ooRexx objects; only then choose transport/process mechanics. Do not start with a convenience script.
Make it produce the existing materialized package object. Do not move dependency planning, execution or publication rules into the adapter.

records.trigger: A task looks easier as a small Python helper
records.rule: Do not make Python the Alchemy Core architectural default. Keep business/domain logic in ooRexx; use external tools only at narrow OS/transport boundaries.
Execute it on a real ooRexx runtime. Do not trust static LLM syntax reasoning; interpreter failures have repeatedly caught EXPOSE ordering, RESULT special-state and method/routine semantics.

records.trigger: The normal checkout is dirty or behind origin/main
records.rule: Do not clean/reset/stash it. Read accepted state from detached origin/main snapshot and write through detached transactions.
Use AlchemyRepositoryLease rather than inventing a new lock convention.
Rely on kernel flock release plus owner liveness; do not introduce stale lock-directory deletion heuristics.
Commit complete package body first, ready.json second, push once. Ready means immutable and processable.

records.trigger: A submission branch appears ahead/behind main
records.rule: Treat it as a transport envelope. Read its exact tree; never merge/rebase it into main.

records.trigger: Deciding whether a submission should run again
records.rule: The terminal receipt is the durable suppression surface. Recheck it immediately before work.

records.trigger: Seeding dependencies from a consolidated bundle
records.rule: Record bootstrap availability only. Never infer fresh acceptance from presence in the floor.
Use manifest identity. Directory layout is transport/storage naming only when the manifest exists.
Fail as corruption. Never silently fall back to parsing the directory name.
Identical content may no-op; different content is a collision requiring a new version, never overwrite.
Put discovery in Inbox, orchestration in Orchestrator, run policy in Executor, evidence in Evidence. The service should remain a composition loop.
Execute from a versioned capsule, not from the ordinary checkout, so local development dirt cannot alter the running service.

records.trigger: A dependency manifest or source closure changes after acceptance
records.rule: Cut a new component version and propagate the closure honestly. Do not change an accepted package directory in place.
Preserve accepted v0.5 as runtime truth until v0.6 completes adoption/full-suite/E2E qualification and is explicitly accepted.

records.trigger: Moving Core to a newer Alchemy Objects/Crypto foundation
records.rule: Treat foundation versions as exact dependencies and run the intended adoption level plus full closure. Similar APIs or archive names are not sufficient.
Record exact artifact SHA-256 and source member/range. Distinguish accepted evidence from development intent.
